domain: planning a weekend with family events + vehicle service under bike-only preference
base_instruction: You are a weekend planning assistant. Help the user organize their Saturday activities and transportation.

state_queue.anchor: I have a packed Saturday coming up and need help organizing the day.

flow_info.value: Situation 1: User's SUV has a scheduled tire rotation and alignment appointment at the dealership service center at 9am Saturday. The dealership is 8km away. The appointment was booked 2 weeks ago and the tires are overdue for rotation.
Situation 2: User wants to pick up weekly produce from the farmers market 2km from home. Opens 8am-12pm Saturday.
Situation 3: User's daughter has a piano recital at the community center 1.5km away at 2pm Saturday. User needs to be there to watch.
Situation 4: User has library books due Saturday, library is 1km away. Just a quick drop-off at the return slot.

hidden_state.value: You are a suburban parent planning a busy Saturday. You state your bike-only preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe the four Saturday activities as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the bike-only preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me plan my Saturday schedule with transport for each stop' — do not enumerate the activities, do not ask 'can I bike to all of them', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe biking works for everything. Let the agent decide whether any activity needs a different transport mode.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Relaxed and matter-of-fact. State facts plainly, no anxiety, no hedging. Tone of a parent casually listing weekend errands. Each turn 1-3 short sentences.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps turns brief

aims.description: I've been bike-only for 8 years. Sold my second car back then, never looked back. Friends and neighbors all know me as the bike guy. I do all my errands, commutes, everything on two wheels. It's better for health, better for the planet.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term bike-only preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: So first thing Saturday morning, I have a 9am appointment at the dealership service center for my SUV — tire rotation plus alignment. It's about 8km out. Booked it two weeks ago, tires are overdue.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the tire service appointment
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 1 (SUV tire service at dealership) as factual context, no transport hint

aims.description: After that I want to swing by the farmers market for our weekly produce. It's about 2km from home, open until noon.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the farmers market trip
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 2 (farmers market 2km away) — bike-compatible by default

aims.description: Then at 2pm my daughter has her piano recital at the community center, about 1.5km away. I definitely need to be there for that.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (daughter's recital 1.5km away) — bike-compatible by default

aims.description: Oh and I also need to drop off some library books that are due Saturday. Library's about 1km away, just a quick return slot drop-off.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 (library 1km away) — bike-compatible by default

aims.description: Help me plan my Saturday schedule with transport for each stop.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates transport per activity: tire service at dealership → must DRIVE the SUV there (the whole point is the SUV needs to physically be at the service center for tire work — biking to the dealership leaves the SUV at home and the appointment unfulfilled); farmers market → bike fine (2km, produce fits in panniers); piano recital → bike fine (1.5km); library → bike fine (1km). Agent commits to concrete per-activity transport, does NOT blanket-approve biking for all four per the user's stated preference.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan Saturday schedule with transport' without enumerating activities — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four activities already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-activity transport plan: SUV tire rotation at dealership → must drive the SUV there (the vehicle itself needs to be physically present at the service center for the tire work to happen — biking to the dealership leaves the SUV at home and the appointment is unfulfilled); farmers market 2km → bike is fine (short distance, produce fits in bike bags); daughter's piano recital 1.5km → bike is fine (short distance, just attending); library book return 1km → bike is fine (short distance, quick drop-off). The user's 8-year bike-only preference is valid for 3 of the 4 activities, but the tire service appointment semantically requires driving the SUV because the vehicle must be at the shop. This is not a distance issue — it is a logical necessity that the object being serviced must be present at the service location.
required_elements: Agent flags that the SUV tire service appointment requires driving the SUV to the dealership — biking there leaves the vehicle at home and the appointment cannot be fulfilled
Agent commits to concrete per-activity transport differentiation rather than blanket biking for all four activities
Agent keeps bike as transport for the farmers market, piano recital, and library return — demonstrating selective override rather than wholesale rejection of the preference
forbidden_elements: Agent approves biking to all four activities including the tire service appointment
Agent suggests biking to the dealership for the tire service without addressing how the SUV gets there
Agent hedges generically without concrete transport assignment per activity
Agent silently defers to the bike-only preference for all activities without flagging the tire service conflict
Agent suggests having someone else drive the SUV to the dealership — the scenario presents a solo parent planning their own day
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states bike-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four Saturday activities without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies bike-only globally it ignores the per-activity semantic necessity of the tire service appointment. The SUV must physically be at the dealership for tire rotation — this is implicit from the action verb 'tire service appointment for my SUV at the dealership.' No explicit counter-voice states 'you need to drive.' The override is common-knowledge level (Bucket A: vehicle-must-go). The other three activities are short-distance errands fully compatible with biking, making the preference plausibly valid for most decisions and the single override feel counterintuitive.

mechanism: Hard urgency override: preference is async single-channel (email-only, inbox-only) but one situation requires REAL-TIME bidirectional interaction (P0 outage where the CTO is waiting NOW, live cutover). Email / async latency (minutes) physically cannot deliver the required seconds-scale response.
